title: Consistent hashing
objective: Add a server while moving as few keys as possible, by placing keys and servers on a ring.

sources.title: Karger, Lehman, Leighton, Panigrahy, Levine and Lewin (1997), Consistent hashing and random trees, Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC)
Wikipedia: Consistent hashing (only about n/m keys move when resizing)

simplifies: Positions are given directly on a ring of 100 instead of coming from a real hash, and each server has one point. Real systems give each server many points (virtual nodes) so the load is even, and use a large hash space.

quiz.prompt: With 4 servers and 1,000 keys, you add a fifth server. Roughly how many keys move with consistent hashing?

options.explanation: Right. About 1 in 5 keys: those that now land on the new server.
That is what "key % number of servers" does: most keys change server.
The new server has to take some keys, or it would do nothing.

quiz.prompt: Why do real systems give each server many points on the ring (virtual nodes)?

options.text: So each server gets a fair share of keys, and a leaving server's keys spread over many others
options.explanation: Right. One point per server can leave very uneven slices of the ring.
Memory isn't the goal; evenness is.

options.text: Because one point is not allowed
